findings.detail: The same English literal now appears twice — as the pre-scrape warning at line 182 and as the thrown fallback error at line 213. The two must stay in sync (an e2e test asserts both the bare string and `${t.common.error}: ${NEED_FIELDS}`), and unlike the rest of this tab it is not routed through `TRANSLATIONS`, so an Arabic user gets an English sentence prefixed by a translated `Error:`. Low because the behaviour is correct and covered by tests; it would rise to medium if the copy diverged between the two sites.
findings.summary: Gate message "Please describe what data to extract…" duplicated as a literal

findings.detail: `/^\/(?:[a-z]{2}(?:-[A-Za-z]{2})?\/)?a\/([A-Za-z0-9-]+)(?:\/|$)/` only accepts a lowercase two-letter language, optionally with a two-letter region. A Fresha URL carrying a script-subtag locale (`/zh-Hant/a/<slug>`) or an uppercase one (`/EN-GB/a/<slug>`, which a user can produce by hand-editing or by a link shortener normalising case) returns `null`. The failure is silent and safe — the link just takes the old page-text route and the user sees only the first category — but it is indistinguishable from "this isn't a Fresha link". Low: all locales Fresha actually serves today match the current pattern.
findings.summary: Locale-segment regex misses uppercase and non-2-letter locale prefixes

findings.detail: `fetchFreshaVenue(freshaVenue, (u, init) => fetch(u, init))` literally matches the `frontend-boundaries.md` trigger "`fetch(` … inside a file under `components/`". Recording the analysis so a future reviewer does not re-raise it: all request construction, headers, timeout/abort and error shaping live in `services/freshaVenueService.ts`; the component supplies only the browser transport, which is the seam the unit tests use to run `fetchFreshaVenue` with no network. That serves the rule's stated purpose ("so the tab can be rendered in a test without a live database") rather than defeating it, and it mirrors the pre-existing `fetchYallaMenu(yalla, targetUrl, (u, init) => fetch(u, init))` on line 63. Not a violation.
findings.summary: `fetch(` appears in a component, but as an injected transport — not a boundary violation

findings.detail: `/(\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?)/` returns the first number in the formatted string. `from SAR 575` is handled correctly (the `from` prefix also sets `Price Note`), but a hypothetical `SAR 50 - SAR 80` would land as `50.00` with an empty `Price Note` — a figure the customer reads as exact. This path is only reached for option rows, where variants carry no numeric `retailPrice`; the captured venue shows Fresha expressing ranges as `from X`, so no such shape exists in the fixture. Recording it because the module's stated contract is "nothing is invented".
findings.summary: `priceFromFormatted` takes the first number, so a range would be written as an exact price

findings.detail: In the "a non-Fresha link is still blocked" case the spec sleeps 1 s and then asserts `asked` is empty. Proving a negative with a fixed sleep is the one shape in this otherwise event-driven suite that can go flaky under CI load (too short) or slow the run down (too long). The rest of the file correctly waits on visible text. Not a defect — the assertion is sound today.
findings.summary: Fixed `waitForTimeout(1_000)` used to assert "nothing was fetched"
